steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Tomorrow?
On the other end of the phone, the councilor's tone is jubilant.

steps.speaker: Councilor
steps.content: Yes, she leaves tomorrow. The departure documents for Ambassador Du Ruo will be delivered to the MBCC later today. After she leaves the Bureau, please vet her residence to ensure the Outlander doesn't leave behind any traps.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She just returned from WhiteSands yesterday. Isn't this arrangement too hasty?

steps.speaker: Councilor
steps.content: Her stay in DisCity was supposed to be a temporary one. Moreover, we've demonstrated enough generosity by letting her return to Eastia without holding her accountable for the hacking of the database.

steps.speaker: Councilor
steps.content: Trust me, Chief, there's no need for further discussion. Before making the decision, we consulted Ambassador Du Ruo herself, and she had no objections.
When you come to verify this with Du Ruo, she's bending over to light incense. Baggage scatters around the room and an open suitcase lies half-packed on the floor.

options: Have you decided to leave tomorrow?

choices.text: Have you decided to leave tomorrow?

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Yes. Will you miss me?

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: After this departure, we probably won't meet again in a long time.
This room in the Bureau has particularly good lighting. It's because she said upon arrival that Eastians needed to bask in the sun every day to gather spiritual energy.
Du Ruo stands in the light. Smoke gathers around her occasionally and quickly dissipates again.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I will make some arrangements so you can come to DisCity anytime.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Thank you, Chief.
Shrouded by lingering smoke, the room falls silent for a moment.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Can I take something from here as a keepsake? I couldn't get that pendant from Eastside that you disliked.
You look around and find nothing you can give her.
She shakes her head.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: I want this.
Du Ruo opens the window, pointing at a branch outside.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: In old Eastian, breaking a willow branch is symbolic of a reluctant farewell. Could you break off a branch for me?

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Just a small one is fine.
You do as told. Du Ruo takes the branch cherishingly.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Thank you... Seeing this branch, I'll remember the experiences we shared in DisCity. It'll make the long journey home less tedious.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Are you sure you don't want to stay for a few more days?

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Why would you want me to stay?
The branch turns in Du Ruo's hands for a while before going still.
The sun rises higher. Du Ruo stands quietly in the room.
Tomorrow, the sun will still shine into the room, but the person living here will be thousands of miles away.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Chief?
She presses you for an answer deliberately.
Before you can speak, someone knocks on the door.

steps.speaker: MBCC Staff
steps.content: Is this Du Ruo's room?

steps.speaker: MBCC Staff
steps.content: These are your departure documents. Please keep them safe.
The MBCC staff member hands over the envelope to Du Ruo briskly and excuses himself.
Seeing your awkward and embarrassed expression, Du Ruo laughs and sighs, then continues to empty the room.
Dust floats in the air. Passing items to each other, you and Du Ruo begin packing up the luggage wordlessly.
Books, clothes, travel documents.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Will you give me a hand like this again in the future?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: That depends on whether you're thinking of crossing DisCity's line again.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: What counts as crossing the line?
Leaning in suddenly, her voice is so soft it's almost a whisper.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: What if I want to learn more about Mania?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I can answer your questions as long as they're within the permitted range.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: What if I simply want to chat with you?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'll pick up your call.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: What if... I can't make it to DisCity anymore?

options: I'll go to Eastia to see you.
The councilors would probably be happy.

choices.text: I'll go to Eastia to see you.
The councilors would probably be happy.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: You know, you're weird. Is it really necessary that we meet?

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Are you implying that you won't be happy?
This time, she doesn't wait for your reply and simply retreats to a safe distance contentedly.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Alright, no more teasing.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Before our next meeting, I'll remember today, and how much you don't want me to go.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: As a mythologist, once all of this dies down, I will certainly make frequent visits to DisCity. I will also come to see you, if that's what you want.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: So, go make those arrangements for me, Chief. In exchange, I'll leave this with you.
She takes out an Eastian-style thread-bound book with no title on the cover.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What is this?

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: My myth book.
She opens it to the first page and hands it to you.
A nation stood, bearing the name of Dis. The atrocity of the god begot the rampage of calamities. One with no fear stepped forth.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: There once existed a state named Dis, which suffered frequent disasters from the god's wrath. Then, a courageous person stood out.
Wronged and affronted, harmed and maltreated. A foreign one came with a deserter's plan. The hero refused, sworn to slay the god.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Misunderstood and defamed, this person endured endless hardships and unfair treatment. An Outlander tried to take this person away, yet the hero chose to stay and kept fighting the disasters.
A fine line of writing lies at the bottom. The ink looks the darkest. It appears to be a fresh remark.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, what about this sentence? What does it mean?
Once again, she smiles slyly.

steps.speaker: Du Ruo
steps.content: Take your time to guess, Chief. We Eastians are very subtle.
"Only now do I realize one cannot quell the mountains and seas."
